title: The entropies of solvation and transfer of ions in the water-ethanol binary system at 298.15 K

segments.text: The entropies of solvation and transfer of ions in aqueous ethanol were determined from the data obtained by measuring the initial and stationary temperature coefficients of the voltage of thermogalvanic circuits with silver-chloride and quinhydrone electrodes in the system HCl-H2O-C2H5OH.
The influence of the composition of the mixed solvent and the nature of the ions on the entropy characteristics was analyzed.

title: Entropy characteristic of solvation and thermal diffusion of hydrogen chloride in water-1-propanol solutions: A thermoelectrochemical determination

segments.text: Thermogalvanic cells with silver chloride and quinhydrone electrodes in the HCl-H2O-1-PrOH system are studied experimentally.
The results are used to determine standard entropies of thermal diffusion transport of hydrogen chloride, entropies of mobile H+ and Cl- ions, and Soret coefficients of the electrolyte at 298 K.
Thermal diffusion entropies and partial molar entropies of said ions in water-1-propanol solutions are calculated within the Agar model.
The results are interpreted with the application of basic concepts of the De Bethune theory concerning thermal diffusion transport in electrolytes.

title: The behavior of higher manganese silicide single crystals under electrochemical treatment

segments.text: For higher manganese silicide single crystals of certain geometry and superstructure orientation, an unusual metallization process is observed.

This anomaly can be associated either with bulk processes similar to thermogalvanic effects or with the carrier redistribution in the near-surface regions that is due to the high thermoelectric power anisotropy and complex crystal structure.

title: USE OF SOLID-ELECTROLYTE CELL AS AN ACTIVE LOW-TEMPERATURE SENSOR

segments.text: A novel type of thermogalvanic temperature sensor using a solid-electrolyte cell is reported.
As compared to normal thermocouples (sensitivity 0.1 mV/K), this sensor has higher sensitivity (0.2 mV/K), is hysteresis free and linear in the low-temperature range.
Various other possible advantages are indicated to make it worth further study.
